newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court to rule Wed on government pay dispute.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court to rule Wed on government pay dispute.

text.p: Brazil's most senior court was due to meet on Wednesday to finish ruling on a pay dispute which the government fears could add billions of dollars to the federal payroll, a court spokesman said.

The Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) was due to meet at 1400 local time/1700 GMT to decide a case brought by 11 civil servants who claim they are entitled to a 28.9 percent pay rise given to the armed forces in 1993, the spokeswoman said.
The civil servants cite a rule that entitles public sector workers to pay rises awarded to state employees in other categories.

Government officials say a victory for the 11 might set a precedent for the entire federal workforce, adding an estimated $7.0 billion to the federal government's payroll spending, which totalled about $42 billion in 1996.
So far, one STF judge has ruled in favor of the civil servants and another has voted against. The court's other eight members are expected to announce their verdicts tomorrow.
